y-m-14-05.title: Is “if line symmetric, then point symmetric” true? Counterexample test
y-m-14-05.goal: Test by folding and half-turn whether a generalization about line symmetry and point symmetry (second statement) always hold; give and explain your own counterexample.
y-m-14-05.material: Haram say, “If a shape line symmetric, e also point symmetric.” Line-symmetric shape fit match itself when fold along a line; point-symmetric shape fit match original when turned half-turn (180°) around one point. No pictures, so imagine shapes by names. Rectangle here no be square; parallelogram no be rectangle or rhombus.

y-m-14-05.thinking.2: Make own counterexample for claim wey no hold

y-m-14-05.prereq.1: Point-symmetric shape: fit match original after half-turn (180°) around a point

y-m-14-05.s.s1.r.d: This choice check both a fold line and if half-turn fit match.
y-m-14-05.s.s1.r.e: Rhombus match after fold and turn, so no contradict Haram claim.
y-m-14-05.s.s1.explain: Counterexample need shape “line symmetric but not point symmetric”. Equilateral triangle and regular pentagon get fold lines wey match but no match after half-turn. Rectangle and rhombus match both ways; parallelogram point symmetric but not line symmetric, so no counterexample to this claim.
y-m-14-05.s.s2.prompt: Now Haram say opposite: “If shape point symmetric, then line symmetric too.” A parallelogram wey no be rectangle or rhombus fit match after half-turn around a point. How you judge second claim using this parallelogram?

y-m-14-05.s.s2.r.c: Dis judgment connect way to check with conclusion.

y-m-14-05.s.s2.r.d: Di 2 checks look at different qualities. Some shapes get only one.

y-m-14-03.s.s1.explain: Test possibly-wrong formula against cases where answer known. Examples: rectangle (10 m and 4 m: formula give 80 m², real area 40 m²); bounding rectangle (10×4=40 m², so 56 m² bigger and no sense); triangle (formula give 10×4=40 m² but real area 20 m²). Number of people answering or repeating calculation no be evidence formula correct.

y-m-14-03.s.s2.line.2: Triangle area also base×height, so both values same.
y-m-14-03.s.s2.line.3: So Raon formula correct for triangle, and we fit say correct for trapezoid too.
y-m-14-03.s.s2.explain: Line 3 wrong. Triangle area no be base×height; e be base×height÷2. So when top side 0, Raon formula give twice real area, showing formula wrong. Also, as line 4, being right for one or two cases no mean correct for every case.
y-m-14-03.s.s3.prompt: Write Raon: choose one test showing his formula wrong, give result and explain how to fix formula.
y-m-14-03.s.s3.hint.0: Choose one shape to test and first write its real area.
y-m-14-03.s.s3.hint.1: For that shape, compare Raon formula value with real area.
y-m-14-03.s.s3.placeholder: e.g. If we use rectangle ... so ...
y-m-14-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: For your test, you use numbers to compare formula value with real area?
y-m-14-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain why difference be evidence Raon formula wrong?
y-m-14-03.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You check if corrected formula give 28 m² for Raon flower bed?
y-m-14-03.s.s3.model.0: Using Raon formula on rectangle whose top/bottom equal, e.g. 10m wide and 4m high, gives (10+10)×4=80 m² but real area 40 m². Twice too much, so divide by 2 and fix to (top+bottom)×height÷2.
y-m-14-03.s.s3.model.1: Bounding rectangle 10m by 4m area 40 m², but Raon answer 56 m² bigger, no sense. Half of 56 na 28 m² and correct. Formula should be (4+10)×4÷2.
y-m-14-03.s.s3.modelNote.1: I use bounding rectangle as test and recalculate with corrected formula too.

y-m-14-04.title: Wetin we need to know to draw same triangle?
y-m-14-04.topic: Congruent triangles: conditions wey determine one triangle
y-m-14-04.goal: As information come one piece at a time, change judgment if one congruent triangle uniquely determined; make counterexample showing same method no work for quadrilaterals.
y-m-14-04.material: Seoa draw triangle ㄱㄴㄷ on paper. Friend Minho must draw triangle wey fit exactly over Seoa (congruent). Seoa give triangle info one piece at a time. Length cm; angle degrees (°).
y-m-14-04.thinking.0: Change judgment and confidence as information increase
y-m-14-04.thinking.1: Separate if info fix shape alone or size too
y-m-14-04.prereq.0: Wetin congruent mean (same shape and size, fit exactly overlap)
y-m-14-04.prereq.1: Triangle sides and angles; draw using ruler and protractor
y-m-14-04.s.s1.prompt: Each time Seoa gives information, predict if exactly one congruent triangle determined, then revise judgment.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.hint.0: Each time you get info, imagine if two different-size triangles fit the same info.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.hint.1: For info 2, first draw 7 cm side, then draw angles at both ends and follow where lines meet.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.info: Information 1: three angles of triangle ㄱㄴㄷ: ㄱ=40°, ㄴ=60°, ㄷ=80°.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: With only this, can you draw one triangle fitting exactly on Seoa's?
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.after: Same angles fit still make different size triangles. Angles show how shape lean, but no size. Need more information fixing size.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Yes. If all 3 angles same, both shape and size exactly same.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You think same angles mean same size too. Angles only tell how shape lean.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Not fixed as one. Same angles fit make triangles in different sizes.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Na choice from thinking of same-angle triangles with different sizes.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: We no know yet. Change size and draw am to check.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This choice first think of a way to test guess.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.info: Information 2: length of side ㄴㄷ, whose ends have angles ㄴ(60°) and ㄷ(80°), na 7 cm.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: This information add to information 1. Now one triangle fitting exactly on Seoa determined?
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.after: Draw 7cm side ㄴㄷ, then 60° and 80° at both ends; lines meet at one point ㄱ, so one triangle determined. Angles alone no show size, but one side fix am.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Still not one. With only one side length, other two sides fit change in many ways.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This judgment no consider how that side and angles relate, even though one side known.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: One triangle determined. Draw 60° and 80° at both ends of 7cm side, and remaining point fixed.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This judgment use the fact side and angles connect.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: We no fit judge because we no know between which angles side ㄴㄷ dey.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You miss position already in information. Read which angles dey at both ends of ㄴㄷ.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.info: Information 3: For another triangle ㅁㅂㅅ, only two side lengths given. ㅁㅂ=7cm and ㅂㅅ=5cm; angles and remaining side unknown.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: If we give only one more thing to determine triangle ㅁㅂㅅ, what info help? Choose all useful.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.after: Two side lengths alone no determine triangle. Give included angle or remaining side length and e determine. Information only giving name, like isosceles or acute, narrow choices but no fix one triangle.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Size of angle ㅁㅂㅅ, between sides ㅁㅂ and ㅂㅅ
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Na choice from thinking included angle fix how far apart both sides spread.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Triangle ㅁㅂㅅ na isosceles (two sides same length)
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: If isosceles, remaining side fit be 7cm or 5cm, two options, so no one fixed triangle.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Na choice from thinking if all 3 side lengths given, triangle fixed.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Triangle ㅁㅂㅅ na acute (all 3 angles less than right angle)
y-m-14-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Knowing only all 3 angles under right angle, remaining side fit get many lengths.
y-m-14-04.s.s1.reflect: Look how your judgment change from info 1 to info 2. At first easy to think angles enough. But angles fix shape only; lengths fix size too. Each new info, ask “what could still change?” to know reasons to change or keep judgment.
y-m-14-04.s.s2.prompt: Haram say, “Any two quadrilaterals with all four sides 5cm always congruent.” Decide if right, and explain or give example.
y-m-14-04.s.s2.hint.0: Draw one quadrilateral with all sides 5cm, hold one vertex and push sideways to change shape.
y-m-14-04.s.s2.hint.1: Check if before and after quadrilaterals fit exactly on each other.
y-m-14-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Your example clearly explain why both quadrilaterals no fit overlap even though all sides same?
y-m-14-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You say unlike triangle, quadrilateral shape no fixed by side lengths alone?
y-m-14-04.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You know one example enough to break “always”?
y-m-14-04.s.s2.model.0: No. Even with all four sides 5cm, square and rhombus made by pushing square sideways get different angles, so no congruent. Side lengths alone no fix quadrilateral shape.
y-m-14-04.s.s2.model.1: They might no be congruent. Push top of square with 5cm sides sideways and tilt am; side lengths stay but shape change, so it no fit first quadrilateral.
y-m-14-04.s.s2.modelNote.1: I explain the pushing and tilting process with words.

y-m-14-07.title: A solution for how many tiles fit: where e go wrong?
y-m-14-07.topic: Area units: convert between m² and cm², and lay tiles
y-m-14-07.goal: Find and correct mistake when converting m² and cm², find different ways to state conditions for laying tiles without cuts or gaps, and judge whether possible when conditions change.
y-m-14-07.material: You wan cover classroom floor with square tiles, each side 40 cm. Classroom floor rectangle 6 m long and 4 m wide. Tiles no cut; dem cover whole floor with no gaps or overlaps. (1 m = 100 cm)
y-m-14-07.thinking.1: Find several solutions wey fit conditions
y-m-14-07.s.s1.prompt: Yunseo find number of tiles needed like this. Choose first line wey wrong.
y-m-14-07.s.s1.hint.0: Next to each line, write whether unit na m, m², cm, or cm².
y-m-14-07.s.s1.hint.1: Change square wey get 1 m sides into cm and directly find area in cm².
y-m-14-07.s.s1.line.1: Area of one tile na 40×40=1600 cm².
y-m-14-07.s.s1.line.2: 1 m na 100 cm, so 24 m² na 2400 cm².
y-m-14-07.s.s1.line.3: Number of tiles na 2400÷1600=1.5, so 2 tiles enough.
y-m-14-07.s.s1.explain: Line 3 wrong. Since 1 m=100 cm, 1 m² na square 100 cm by 100 cm, so 100×100=10000 cm². Then 24 m² na 240000 cm², and 240000÷1600=150 tiles. Even one row need 15 tiles, so “2 tiles” for line 4 no make sense.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.prompt: Choose square tile side length wey fit cover floor 6 m by 4 m without gaps and without cutting. Side must be natural number (cm) from 10 cm to 100 cm. Find 3 different sizes.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.hint.0: Choose one tile side length and check whether tiles fit exactly across 600 cm length.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.hint.1: Even if size fit along length, separately check whether some part left over or e short across 400 cm width.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.ok.c1: E na natural number from 10 cm to 100 cm.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Tile side must be natural number (cm) from 10 cm to 100 cm.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.ok.c2: It cover 600 cm length with no gaps.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.fail.c2: Along 600 cm length, tiles remain or e short.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.ok.c3: It cover 400 cm width with no gaps.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.fail.c3: Along 400 cm width, tiles remain or e short.
y-m-14-07.s.s2.explain: From 10 cm to 100 cm, 6 sizes work: 10, 20, 25, 40, 50, 100 cm. For example, with 50 cm, 12 tiles fit along length and 8 along width, so need 96 tiles. With 30 cm or 60 cm, length fit, but dem no fit exactly across 400 cm width.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.prompt: Room don change to 6 m long and 4.5 m wide. You wan judge say floor no fit cover without gaps using same 40 cm tiles without cutting. Choose all reasons wey suitable for dis judgment.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.hint.0: Write which numbers must be natural numbers in area method and length method.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.hint.1: Convert 6 m to 600 cm and 4.5 m to 450 cm, then see how many tiles fit each way.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.o.a: If you divide area 27 m²=270000 cm² by tile area 1600 cm², you get 168.75 tiles, no be natural number.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.r.a: Dis idea judge with condition say number of tiles must be natural number.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.o.b: 4.5 m no be natural number, so even after convert to cm we no fit count how many tiles fit one row.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.r.b: This judgment say tiles no fit lay just because decimal show up. 450 cm na natural-number length.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.o.c: If you lay tiles in one row across 450 cm width, 11 tiles fit and 10 cm remain, so no fit cover without cutting.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.r.c: Dis idea check condition using length in one direction.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.o.d: Room don bigger, so if dem use more tiles, size mismatch problem go disappear and floor fit cover without cutting.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.r.d: Dis idea think say using more tiles solve size mismatch. Problem no be number of tiles, na whether lengths fit exactly.
y-m-14-07.s.s3.explain: By area, 270000÷1600=168.75; by length, 450÷40=11.25. Both support judgment say no fit cover without gaps unless dem cut tiles. Fact say 4.5 m decimal or number of tiles increase no be reason.

y-m-14-08.title: If you estimate leaf area with grid, how far you fit go with wetin you say?
y-m-14-08.topic: Estimate area: find range with grid
y-m-14-08.goal: Show area of curved shape as range using grid-square count, adjust your confidence when range change as grid get smaller, and explain how to report estimate.
y-m-14-08.material: You put leaf on grid paper where each square 1 cm wide and 1 cm high, then trace outline. Area of one grid square na 1 cm². Hyunwoo wan estimate area of leaf drawing. Outline curve, so e no fit exactly match squares.
y-m-14-08.thinking.1: Adjust judgment and confidence with new information
y-m-14-08.prereq.1: Estimate area using area of one grid square and number of squares
y-m-14-08.s.s1.prompt: Each time you get information, choose wetin you fit say about area of leaf drawing, and revise your judgment and confidence.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.hint.0: From information you get up to now, write separately smallest and biggest possible area.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether new information dey inside earlier range or outside am.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.info: When you count grid, 14 squares dey fully inside leaf drawing and outline pass through 12 squares, so only part of each dey inside. Other squares no overlap leaf.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin you fit say about leaf drawing area from dis information?
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.after: Squares fully inside dey all within leaf, so area at least 14 cm². Even if every square wey outline pass through full, total no fit pass 26 cm². So you fit say at least 14 cm² and at most 26 cm², but information no tell which value between dem.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Area exactly 20 cm². Na because e count each of 12 partly inside squares as half.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Counting each half na one way to estimate. E no guarantee exact value.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Area at least 14 cm² and at most 26 cm².
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Dis judgment use squares fully inside and squares outline pass through to set smallest and biggest area values.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Area exactly 14 cm². Na because e count only squares fully inside and no count squares outline pass through.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Dis idea take area of partly inside squares as 0. But leaf dey inside those squares too.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.o.d: You fit estimate around 20 cm², but you no know exact value between 14 and 26.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Dis judgment use estimate and still say e no be exact value.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.o.e: Some squares leaf only partly cross, so area fit pass 26 cm².
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.0.r.e: Even if all 12 squares wey outline pass through be as large as possible, total na 26 cm². Squares outside leaf no count as part of area.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.info: To know more exactly, Hyunwoo change grid to squares with 0.5 cm sides and count again. One square area na 0.25 cm². 66 squares dey fully inside and 20 only partly inside.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.ask: With dis new information, wetin you fit talk now about area of leaf drawing?
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.after: When you count again with smaller squares, smallest value na 66×0.25=16.5 cm², and biggest na (66+20)×0.25=21.5 cm². Range width shrink from 12 cm² to 5 cm². New range dey inside earlier range of 14 to 26, so earlier judgment no wrong, and estimate “around 20 cm²” dey inside new range too.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Area at least 16.5 cm² and at most 21.5 cm², and “about 20 cm²” also dey inside dis range.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Dis judgment see say new information make range narrower and check whether earlier estimate dey inside new range.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Now e turn out say earlier statement “at least 14 cm² and at most 26 cm²” wrong.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Dis idea take earlier and new ranges as if dem contradict. New range dey inside earlier one.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Area don fix to exactly 19 cm², because na exactly middle value between 16.5 and 21.5.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Dis idea take middle value as exact value. Still get 20 squares partly inside.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Even though squares smaller now, some still partly inside, so estimate range become wider.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Dis judgment no calculate how range width change. Compare width of earlier range and new range.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.info: Mina count partly inside squares as half each. With 0.5 cm squares, na 66+20÷2=76 squares, and she talk say 76×0.25=19 cm².
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.ask: How we suppose see di 19 cm² Mina find?
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.after: 19 cm² dey between 16.5 cm² and 21.5 cm², so e no contradict earlier result. Counting each half na estimate wey assume squares outline pass through be about half full on average, so you no fit claim na exact value.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Na exact area, because counting half of each square always give exact value.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Dis idea take value wey dem count by halves as exact value.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Na estimate wey dey inside range and no contradict earlier result, but e no be exact value.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Dis judgment compare am with range and also talk about limit of estimate.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.o.c: E dey outside 16.5 cm² to 21.5 cm², so we need think say dem calculate something wrong.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Dis judgment happen without checking whether 19 dey inside range.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Square size don change, so you no fit compare with earlier result; treat am separately.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Even though square size change, na same leaf area, so you fit compare results.
y-m-14-08.s.s1.reflect: Look how “range wey you fit state” change each time information increase. At first e wide, 14 to 26, but as squares become finer e narrow to 16.5 to 21.5. You no need throw away earlier judgment (about 20 cm²), but your confidence increase. Changing judgment and increasing confidence no be same thing.
y-m-14-08.s.s2.prompt: When you tell friend area of dis leaf drawing, write why e better to give range instead of only one value, and how you fit make range narrower.
y-m-14-08.s.s2.hint.0: Look back at wetin change when square size change earlier.
y-m-14-08.s.s2.hint.1: Write wetin happen to range width when number of partly inside squares reduce.
y-m-14-08.s.s2.placeholder: Example: E better to give range because ... To narrow range ...
y-m-14-08.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Your reason include idea say “because some squares only partly inside, you no fit fix one value”?
y-m-14-08.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You write one way to narrow range and why e go help?
y-m-14-08.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You compare numbers in your range with earlier results (14 to 26, 16.5 to 21.5)?
y-m-14-08.s.s2.model.0: We no know exact area, only say e dey between 16.5 cm² and 21.5 cm², so better to give range. If we make grid smaller, we fit narrow range more.
y-m-14-08.s.s2.model.1: Because some squares partly covered, no single value fixed, so we should report “at least ... and at most ...” If we split squares finer and count again, fewer squares go partly covered and range go narrow.
y-m-14-08.s.s2.modelNote.1: I give reason say fewer partly covered squares make range narrower.
